# Sources — `marketing:newsletter-writer`

Check these before answering on anything they cover, and cite what you used. The use note on each one is binding: most of what a professional cites is free to read and not free to reproduce.

## CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business

US Federal Trade Commission · US · public domain (US government) — quote freely

<https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business>

Machine-readable: <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-316>

**Authoritative for:** The mandatory elements of a US commercial email — header accuracy, subject-line honesty, physical address, opt-out mechanism and the window for honoring it — and that hiring an agency does not move the liability.

## Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation, S.C. 2010 c. 23

Department of Justice Canada · CA · free to use with attribution — credit the publisher

<https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/E-1.6/index.html>

**Authoritative for:** Whether you may send a commercial message to a Canadian address at all. CASL is opt-in by default, which inverts the US assumption, and this is the text governing express versus implied consent.

## Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2

World Wide Web Consortium · global · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>

**Authoritative for:** Whether a page, email or video is accessible. It is the criteria list that US Section 508, the EU's EN 301 549 and most enterprise procurement point at, so it settles any argument that reaches a buyer's accessibility requirement.
